scope: Targeted primary-source review of scalable LLM multi-task policy updates and implications for the pinned Motus/RLinf RoboTwin study; not an exhaustive novelty search or a launched experiment

decisions.pcgrad_role: Completed two-task directional intervention and engineering reference; do not promote to the default large-task method without evidence of benefit
decisions.grpo_role: Candidate advantage estimator and clipped online policy objective, orthogonal to task-gradient combination; not an automatic multi-task conflict solution
decisions.current_pipeline: Frozen offline data, shared critic labels and native weighted FM. FM loss is not an action log probability; do not relabel this as GRPO
decisions.priority: First verify functional interference through controlled removal of the other task loss and actual post-update losses, then closed-loop replication. Investigate sampling or update constraints only when their proposed mediator is present
decisions.online_boundary: GRPO interaction/likelihood qualification is a separate online branch. Old offline datasets lack same-initial-condition rollout groups and validated behavior log probabilities. No new rollouts or training launched by this review

papers.name: PCGrad
papers.reading_scope: Method and task-gradient projection; used by completed local implementation
papers.mechanism: Collect per-task gradients and project negatively aligned directions before combination
papers.scaling: Naive dense all-task storage O(TP), pairwise surgery O(T^2 P); sampled task subsets, sharding and approximations change the practical cost. T denotes tasks present in the update, not necessarily every task in the dataset
papers.local_limit: Completed local norm-matched variant gives no robust closed-loop gain. Raw projection properties are not guarantees after group clipping, learning rates and AdamW

papers.name: GRPO / DeepSeekMath
papers.reading_scope: Section4.1, outcome-supervision group-relative baseline and clipped policy objective
papers.mechanism: Generate multiple responses for the same prompt; replace learned value baseline with within-group reward comparisons
papers.borrow: A critic-free baseline with verifiable outcomes can test dependence on learned value estimates
papers.limit: Still needs reward and appropriate behavior-policy rollouts and likelihood ratios; reward-relative advantage is zero for equal-reward groups. Same prompt corresponds to same task/instruction and controlled initial condition, not arbitrary different tasks

papers.name: DAPO
papers.mechanism: Asymmetric clipping, filter equal-outcome groups and resample, token-level loss aggregation
papers.borrow: Track zero-advantage filtering, effective task exposure, clipping fraction and normalization denominators
papers.limit: Resampling costs additional interaction and may change task proportions; language token-length recipes cannot be assumed correct for action dimensions/chunks

papers.name: Dr. GRPO
papers.mechanism: Remove response-length and reward-standard-deviation normalization terms to address the analyzed optimization biases
papers.borrow: Audit whether normalization changes effective sample/task weighting independently of gradient direction
papers.limit: LLM optimization-bias analysis is not direct evidence about this native masked-FM implementation

papers.name: MT-GRPO
papers.reading_scope: Sections2,4,5 and AppendixD.2/D.4/D.5; objective equivalence and proofs not independently verified
papers.mechanism: Improvement-aware task weights and acceptance-aware ratio-preserving sampling after zero-advantage filtering
papers.borrow: Separate intended task weights from realized post-filtering sample proportions. Counterfactual ablation should separate reweighting and ratio preservation
papers.scaling: Task-level scalars and one weighted actor backward avoid storing full per-task parameter gradients; sampling can still add substantial rollout cost
papers.limit: Reasoning benchmarks with3B/7B models and3/9-task settings do not establish continuous-control benefits. Preserved batch counts are not equal gradient magnitudes. Our completed gradient study already matches256 effective draws/task, so filtering imbalance cannot simply be asserted as its cause

papers.name: GSPO
papers.reading_scope: Sequence-level ratio/clipping design and reported MoE stability motivation
papers.mechanism: Sequence-level importance weighting and clipping rather than token-level ratios
papers.borrow: Align reward unit, policy-ratio unit and update aggregation; log clipping and distribution drift by task
papers.limit: Not a task-conflict solver. A language response is not automatically equivalent to a denoising path, robot action chunk or environment trajectory; definitions must be derived and tested

papers.name: EPPO
papers.reading_scope: Sections4-5, task entropy tracking and clipping; authors explicitly distinguish entropy from learning progress
papers.mechanism: Adapt per-task clipping from relative entropy pace and constrain destabilizing trends
papers.borrow: Look for task-dependent update pace and drift before introducing per-task update constraints
papers.limit: Agentic LLM results are not VLA proof; continuous-action marginal entropy is not token entropy or injected diffusion noise entropy. Current FM objective has no PPO clipping ratio

papers.name: piRL
papers.reading_scope: Flow-SDE/Flow-Noise likelihood construction, algorithm comparison and AppendixF.1/Table9
papers.mechanism: Stochastic flow sampling supports online policy optimization for pi0/pi0.5
papers.reported_comparison: Table9 reports pi0.5 LIBERO average77.1 SFT,91.5 GRPO,97.9 PPO within the paper's setup; not local Motus/RoboTwin results or proof PPO always wins
papers.borrow: Use pinned official RLinf probability/sampling infrastructure if opening an online branch, with matched model/sampler/data budgets
papers.limit: Online exploration, policy family and likelihood paths differ from current fixed offline weighted-FM experiment

papers.name: ARFM
papers.mechanism: Adapt RL weighting strength in an offline flow-matching objective
papers.borrow: A closer comparator for offline FM than directly transplanting token-based GRPO. Monitor weight concentration and effective sample size
papers.limit: Does not by itself establish multi-task interference or instruction-aware updates; adaptive weighting is already prior work

papers.name: Generalist robot policy improvement
papers.reading_scope: Abstract/introduction and experimental taxonomy; detailed new ablations not re-audited in this review
papers.mechanism: Studies online generalist improvement across task diversity with value estimation, policy extraction and resource allocation controls
papers.borrow: Scale trained-task diversity and untrained-task retention separately; compare learning and extraction recipes
papers.limit: Multi-task improvement and critic-guided extraction are established research directions, not novelty of this project; its online evidence is not a fixed-offline-budget result

local_scale_calculation.scope: Arithmetic estimate for this unsharded implementation only; excludes model/optimizer/activations and does not claim50 tasks must all appear in each minibatch

local_code_review.status: Relevant components exist in the pinned source. A matched Motus/RoboTwin multi-task GRPO recipe is not yet qualified; no source or training config changed

proposed_tests.name: Matched other-task loss removal
proposed_tests.design: Clone one common model/optimizer state and matched2A+2B data/noise. Compare A-only, B-only and joint by zeroing the other loss while retaining parameter groups and the common denominator; repeat fixed batches and seeds. Add common actual-parameter-step-norm diagnostic, report output drift separately; use a fixed nonzero probe learning rate
proposed_tests.measure: Actual before/after train losses and held-out successful-trajectory FM error by task, separately from first-order estimates and closed-loop success
proposed_tests.interpretation: Off-diagonal held-out surrogate loss increase alongside own-task improvement is functional interference for that surrogate. It is not yet proof of lower robot success
proposed_tests.followup: Only if an effect repeats, compare short matched task-only/joint trajectories and paired closed-loop outcomes. Existing successful-BC task-mixing study is not this fixed-critic loss-removal intervention

proposed_tests.name: Effective supervision and update budget
proposed_tests.design: Track requested/retained/masked/clipped supervision, physical action timesteps, instruction coverage and reference-policy output drift by task. Intervene on one verified imbalance: post-filter task quotas, bounded task loss weights, or reference-velocity/action distillation
proposed_tests.controls: Same frozen data and effective update budget, plus a simpler smaller-global-update control. Frozen-flow velocity/action distillation is not exact KL. Equal task exposure and equal gradient norms are different interventions
proposed_tests.stop_rule: Do not repeat balancing when the proposed mediator is already matched or no measurable interference exists

proposed_tests.name: GRPO feasibility before training
proposed_tests.host: local2GPU; online branch requires separate frozen protocol
proposed_tests.design: First qualify the stochastic flow sampler and unmodified-policy logprob ratios, action/chunk masks and reset grouping. Then use the same frozen actor and sampler on8 training initial conditions/task,4 independent policy-noise rollouts/condition,2 tasks:64 episodes. Never group different instructions/initial conditions as if they were the same prompt
proposed_tests.measure: Binary success distribution, equal-outcome group fraction, retained groups/task, rollout/reset time and likelihood consistency; no parameter updates
proposed_tests.analytic_sanity_check: For independent binary outcomes with same success probability p and group size G, informative group probability is1-p^G-(1-p)^G; e.g. G4,p.1 gives.3438 and p.5 gives.875. Real correlated rollouts must be measured
proposed_tests.followup: If viable, compare Flow-SDE PPO and GRPO on matched initial policy/sampler/interactions and online success-replay baseline. Add ratio-preserving task sampling only if filtering imbalance is observed. Count discarded rollouts in costs

proposed_tests.name: Scale and retention confirmation
proposed_tests.design: Predefine4-6 training tasks and untrained-task anchors,3 actor seeds, common interaction/update budgets and final checkpoints. Confirm only a candidate supported by local evidence; no dense50-task PCGrad buffers
proposed_tests.measure: Mean/worst-task performance, per-task gains and losses, retention, effective exposure and total compute/interaction costs

novelty_boundary: Task reweighting, ratio-preserving sampling, entropy-adaptive clipping, gradient surgery, parameter routing and offline adaptive weighted FM are prior mechanisms. A credible contribution requires a demonstrated VLA-specific failure, a discriminating intervention and generalization/retention evidence; none is established by this review

sft_rl_handoff_followup.scope: Abstract-level primary-source follow-up; algorithms and proofs not fully audited
sft_rl_handoff_followup.user_goal: Coordinate multi-task SFT and RL to reduce harmful interference and improve SFT-to-RL warm start; not choose one regime

sources.name: ReFT
sources.relevance: SFT warmup followed by PPO is an established pipeline; not novelty

sources.name: PRISM
sources.relevance: Data allocation across SFT and RL using training dynamics is prior work on LLM agents

sources.name: SFT-to-RL plasticity handoff
sources.relevance: Studies excessive SFT and impaired later RL learnability in language models; a stronger SFT endpoint is not sufficient evidence of better RL preparation

sources.name: Unified training
sources.relevance: Combining static and model-generated data under a unified training objective is prior work; does not validate the proposed VLA mechanism

sft_rl_handoff_followup.experiment_boundary: Stage-factorial ordinary/coordinatedSFT x ordinary/coordinatedRL; critic preparation initially fixed and separately ablated with same actor. Standard post-SFT critic fitting is retained,not replaced by random-criticRL. Separate starting actor performance,critic readiness,RL curves,total preparation costs and capability retention. No new experiments launched.
